## AI that does more than chat.

Hand the boring stuff to AI, so you can focus on what matters. Connect your apps, decide what it can touch, and let it get to work.

**Flagship.** NyxBot, the main agent, lives inside NyxID.

[Try NyxID](https://nyx.chrono-ai.fun/){.btn .btn-primary} [Current documentation](https://nyx.chrono-ai.fun/docs)

## Technical overview

The following describes the gateway architecture. Available workflows and setup steps depend on the current release; consult the documentation before installation.

## What NyxID Does

Your AI agents can't reach your services. Your internal APIs, localhost dev servers, and private infrastructure are invisible to cloud AI agents.

NyxID is the open-source Agent Connectivity Gateway. One gateway between your APIs and your AI agents. Built in Rust. Self-hosted.

::: {.features-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Credential-Injecting Proxy

NyxID sits between your agents and your APIs as a reverse proxy. When an agent makes a request, NyxID auto-injects the correct credentials at the network layer. With services configured for gateway injection, agents can call them without receiving the raw API keys.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### NAT Traversal

Your internal APIs and dev servers can be reached by AI agents through SSH tunnels. No public endpoint, no firewall changes, no VPN.

Run `nyxid node start` to expose private services to your agents.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### REST → MCP Auto-Wrap

Point NyxID at any REST API. NyxID generates an MCP Server that any MCP-compatible client can consume. The generated MCP interface can be used by compatible clients.
:::
:::

## How It Works

```
Your Services (localhost / internal APIs / any REST endpoint)
  ↓
NyxID Gateway
  ├── Credential Injection (reverse proxy auto-injects keys per request)
  ├── NAT Traversal (SSH tunnels — expose private services)
  ├── MCP Auto-Wrap (REST → MCP Server, auto-generated)
  └── Per-Agent Isolation (scoped tokens, agents can't see each other)
  ↓
Any AI Agent (Claude Code / Cursor / n8n / any MCP client)
```


## Skills across runtimes

[Ornn](ornn.qmd) is a separate skill lifecycle API: find, install, run, build and share skills across runtimes. Project availability and integrations vary; this overview does not promise automatic provisioning or cross-device synchronization.
